chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Abu Abdullah al-Jamourani, from Suleiman al-Ja'fari, who said:

I heard Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying: 'Do not kill the grouse, and do not eat its flesh, for it is frequent in glorification. It says at the end of its glorification: "May Allah curse those who hate the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon them)."'

key_terms.التَّسْبِيحِ: Glorification (of God), referring to the bird's vocalizations
key_terms.الْقُنْبُرَةَ: The grouse, a type of bird mentioned in this hadith

ai.seo_question: Why is it prohibited to eat the flesh of the grouse in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) in *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Shia concept of *tasbih al-khalq*, where creation glorifies God, extending this to the grouse's specific declaration of cursing enemies of the Ahl al-Bayt. It serves as a theological basis for the permissibility or preference of eating the bird, linking zoological traits to creedal loyalty. The hadith highlights the unique status of the Ahl al-Bayt within the cosmic order, where even animals bear witness to their enmity.
